subject: Burst credit allocation causing invoice delta — Acme Cloud Solutions
messages:
From: aws-marketplace-billing@amazonaws.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: billing@acmecloud.com
Date: Sun, 03 Aug 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: burst credit allocation impacting metered usage window (Acme Cloud Solutions)

Hi Redwood team,

AWS Marketplace Billing Ops here — we detected a pattern on 2025-07-31 where the burst-credit smoothing step in our post-processing pipeline reallocated credits across adjacent hourly windows for a subset of seller-meter IDs. In a handful of cases this produced lower per-hour reported consumption compared to raw meter ticks, which can cause an apparent undercharge on the generated invoice.

We pulled a sample of affected meter lines for Acme (attached: metering_sample_20250731.csv). The rows show meter_id, timestamp_utc, reported_units, credit_adjustment, and final_units. Initial spot checks indicate credits were applied at aggregate (project) level instead of per-meter-instance for the 01:00–04:00 UTC window.

Can Redwood provide a mapping from your invoice lines to the raw meter IDs and the per-hour consumption you used for billing? If you can re-run a UTC-hour re-aggregation with credits applied at the meter_id granularity, that should align totals. If helpful, we can also provide the full raw export for that day.

Next steps we propose:
- Confirm timeframe (we are focused on 2025-07-31 00:00–06:00 UTC)
- Exchange raw usage exports (we can provide an S3 presigned export)
- Coordinate a short reconciliation call (30 min) to agree on corrected invoice numbers or short-term crediting approach

Attachment: metering_sample_20250731.csv (CSV, 120KB)

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Billing Ops
aws-marketplace-billing@amazonaws.com
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: michael.ross@acmecloud.com, aws-marketplace-billing@amazonaws.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 03 Aug 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: burst credit allocation impacting metered usage window (Acme Cloud Solutions)

Thanks for the heads-up and the sample export — appreciate the quick flag.

Synthesis / immediate asks:
1) Confirming timeframe: 2025-07-31 00:00–06:00 UTC (we'll widen to 00:00–12:00 UTC for safety).
2) Michael: can you attach the invoice you saw the delta on and the customer-facing pairing you have? That will help us map invoice_line_id -> meter_id.
3) AWS: if you can send the full raw export for the full UTC day (presigned S3 link is perfect) we will: a) re-aggregate per UTC hour at meter_id granularity, b) reapply credits at meter level, c) produce a corrected invoice stub and a delta table.

I've attached our quick triage playbook (playbook-checklist.xlsx) and assigned an internal owner (Karthik) to lead the reconciliation. Proposed timeline: raw exports in 24 hours -> internal triage in 48 hours -> recon call in 72 hours. Please confirm availability for a 30-min slot tomorrow 09:00–13:00 PT.

Soojín Lee
Billing Operations | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Notice: burst credit allocation impacting metered usage window (Acme Cloud Solutions)

Soojín — thanks. Attaching the pairing doc we used to reconcile the July invoice: invoice-pairing_ACME-JUL.pdf.

Quick context: our finance team noticed ~USD 12,400 in missing charges on the July 31 invoice when comparing their internal telemetry to Redwood's invoice lines (same dataset we submitted during onboarding). We did not expect burst-credit smoothing to move credits across hours — that behavior does change how we recognize consumption for committed discount bands.

We can be available for a call tomorrow 11:00 PT. Also happy to upload any additional logs.

—Michael Ross
Head of Cloud Economics, Acme Cloud Solutions
michael.ross@acmecloud.com
Attachment: invoice-pairing_ACME-JUL.pdf (PDF, 210KB)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, michael.ross@acmecloud.com, aws-marketplace-billing@amazonaws.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 Aug 2025 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: burst credit allocation impacting metered usage window (Acme Cloud Solutions)

Thanks all — I pulled the sample and did a quick spike. Short summary of what I'm seeing (high level):
- Root cause hypothesis: the AWS post-process aggregated credits at the project level before distributing adjustments back to meter rows. For meters that cross short high-throughput bursts (e.g., autoscaled jobs), the rounding/assignment step can push credits into adjacent UTC hours.
- Effect: per-hour tallies used for invoice banding/committed discounts can differ materially (we're seeing ~0.5–1.2% divergence in most sellers, but ACME hit a concentrated burst window that amplifies to the reported delta).

Proposed technical approach (how Redwood will reconcile):
1) Accept AWS raw export (UTC timestamps) and ACME's invoice pairing file.
2) Run re-aggregation at meter_id + UTC hour granularity (no project-level smoothing).
3) Reapply credits strictly at the meter_id row level and compute final_units per hour.
4) Produce: (a) a delta table mapping invoice_line_id -> corrected_units -> corrected_charge, (b) a corrected invoice stub, and (c) a short-term credit memo recommendation if delta > $1,000.

I attached the SQL we plan to run so ACME / AWS can review (reconciliation-query.sql). If everyone agrees, we'll spin up the job and share preliminary numbers in 24 hours.

On scheduling: tomorrow 11:00 PT works for Redwood (I've tentatively added the calendar invite).

-Karthik
Principal — Marketplace Revenue Engineering | Redwood Inference
Attachment: reconciliation-query.sql (SQL, 6KB)
